## Why this matters: five results that looked right {#why}

::: {.lever-box}
[Each session had a result that passed the obvious test, and the evidence that decided it]{.label}

| Session | Looked right | What decided |
|---|---|---|
| 2 · VLE | weighted NRTL, RMS(r/σ) = 1.16 | predicts a split at x₁ = 0.088–0.237 in a miscible liquid |
| 3 · LLE | exact fit to one tie line | held-out tie lines: 0.077 with constant τ, 0.0097 with a + b/T |
| 4 · SLE | W = +238 J/mol, naphthalene–benzene | other fusion data give W = −522; the prediction is unchanged |
| 5 · reaction | the solver converged | K from constant Δ<sub>r</sub>H° gives 0.498 conversion; correct K gives 0.795 |
| 6 · cell | γ± fitted to ±0.022 in ln γ | the cell needs (mγ±)²; without the square every EMF is half |
:::

In each case, a small residual was the wrong test. The question was always which evidence the claim needed.

## One condition, six forms {#forms}

| Session | Working equation | What the model supplies |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · VLE, flash | y<sub>i</sub>Φ<sub>i</sub>P = x<sub>i</sub>γ<sub>i</sub>P<sub>i</sub><sup>sat</sup>; Σz<sub>i</sub>(K<sub>i</sub> − 1)/[1 + β(K<sub>i</sub> − 1)] = 0 | γ, P<sup>sat</sup> |
| 2 · measured VLE | γ<sub>i</sub> = y<sub>i</sub>Φ<sub>i</sub>P/(x<sub>i</sub>P<sub>i</sub><sup>sat</sup>) | G<sup>E</sup> model and its weights |
| 3 · LLE | x<sub>i</sub><sup>α</sup>γ<sub>i</sub><sup>α</sup> = x<sub>i</sub><sup>β</sup>γ<sub>i</sub><sup>β</sup>; TPD(w) ≥ 0 | τ(T) |
| 4 · SLE, adsorption | ln(x₁γ₁) = −(Δ<sub>fus</sub>H/R)(1/T − 1/T<sub>m</sub>); n = PV/RT + mq(P) | fusion data, W; isotherm |
| 5 · reactions | $\prod_i(y_i\hat\varphi_iP/P^\circ)^{\nu_i}=K(T)$ | H(T), S(T), K<sub>φ</sub> |
| 6 · cells | E = −Δ<sub>r</sub>G/nF; a<sub>KCl</sub> = (mγ±)² | γ±(m), its T dependence |

Every row is μ<sub>i</sub> equal across phases, or Σν<sub>i</sub>μ<sub>i</sub> = 0. What changes is the reference state and the model.

## The evidence ladder {#ladder}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.lever-box}
[Weakest to strongest]{.label}

| Rung | Course example |
|---|---|
| 1 · calibration | one tie line, exactly |
| 2 · consistency | O/C ratio closes; TPD ≥ 0 at both liquids |
| 3 · held-out | fit 60 kPa, check 80 kPa: 0.164 |
| 4 · independent property | LLE data rule out a VLE-fitted split |
| 5 · different method | calorimetry for ∂ln γ±/∂T |
:::
:::
::: {.column width="48%" .rule-notes}
A claim is only as strong as the highest rung it reached.

**Extrapolation reaches none:** the a + b/T model's gap closing at 324 K lies beyond the last tie line at 316 K.

**Some claims cannot be reached with the data in hand:** the sign of W for naphthalene–benzene, or dγ±/dT from KCl data with expanded uncertainty U = 0.03.

[Saying so is part of the answer.]{.q}
:::
::::

## Where does each claim sit? {#activity-1 .activity}

[Activity 1 · 10 minutes · alone, then with a partner]{.act-label}

::: {.prompt}
Place each claim on the ladder, or mark it as an extrapolation or not resolvable with these data:
:::

1. The weighted 60 kPa NRTL fit is right because RMS(r/σ) = 1.16.
2. Fit at 60 kPa, the model checks at 80 kPa with RMSE 0.164 in ln γ.
3. NRTL with α = 0.3 reproduces the 298.15 K tie line exactly.
4. Cyclohexane and methanol become fully miscible at 324 K.
5. Naphthalene + benzene deviates positively from ideal.
6. For KCl, γ± at 1 mol/kg rises by 0.004 between 298 and 308 K.

::: {.selfstudy}
**On your own:** pause here and write your answer. In place of a partner, compare it with the next slide and write one sentence on any difference and its cause.
:::

## Activity 1: check your answer {#activity-1-debrief}

| Claim | Where it sits | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · RMS(r/σ) = 1.16 | calibration | it describes the fitting data; the same fit predicts a false split |
| 2 · checks at 80 kPa | held-out | different pressure, not used in the fit |
| 3 · exact tie line | calibration | two equations, two unknowns |
| 4 · miscible at 324 K | extrapolation | beyond the last tie line at 316.15 K |
| 5 · positive deviation | not resolvable | the sign follows the fusion data set |
| 6 · rise of 0.004 | not resolvable | far inside U = 0.03 |

Two of six claims are calibration presented as validation, and two cannot be decided with these data. That ratio is typical of real reports.

## Problem A · a flash that returns one liquid {#problem-a}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.prompt}
Cyclohexane (1) + methanol (2) at 298.15 K, NRTL with α = 0.3, τ₁₂ = 1.851, τ₂₁ = 1.433. A flash at z₁ = 0.25 returns one liquid. Is that the equilibrium? If not, what are the phases and their amounts?
:::

Sessions 1 and 3.
:::
::: {.column width="48%" .rule-notes}
[Hints]{.label}

1. Curvature at z₁: positive or negative?
2. TPD over the whole range of w, not from the feed.
3. Binodal from opposite sides of the spinodal.
4. Lever rule.
:::
::::

## Problem B · a crystallizer {#problem-b}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.prompt}
Naphthalene in octane, saturated at 298.15 K, is cooled to 285 K. Use the NIST fusion data (353.39 K, 19.0 kJ/mol) and W = 2509 J/mol. What fraction of the dissolved naphthalene crystallizes? What would an ideal-solution design have predicted?
:::

Session 4.
:::
::: {.column width="48%" .rule-notes}
[Hints]{.label}

1. Solve ln x₁ + (W/RT)(1 − x₁)² = −(Δ<sub>fus</sub>H/R)(1/T − 1/T<sub>m</sub>) at both T.
2. Basis 1 mol of feed; octane does not crystallize.
3. Is 285 K inside the measured range?
:::
::::

## Problem C · which error matters most? {#problem-c}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.prompt}
Steam reforming at 1100 K, 2000 kPa, S/C = 3 gives 0.795 CH₄ conversion. Rank by effect on the conversion: (i) K from constant Δ<sub>r</sub>H; (ii) the pressure term (P/P°)<sup>Δν</sup> omitted, as if P = P°; (iii) S/C raised to 4; (iv) adding K<sub>φ</sub>.
:::

Then: a KCl cell pair at 0.01 / 1.0 mol/kg is computed with RT/F. By what factor is it wrong?

Sessions 5 and 6.
:::
::: {.column width="48%" .rule-notes}
[Hints]{.label}

1. Use Lab 12 E for each case; change one thing at a time.
2. K<sub>φ</sub> at 1100 K and 2 MPa: ln K<sub>φ</sub> = 0.011 for R1, 0.005 for R2.
3. a<sub>KCl</sub> = (mγ±)².
:::
::::

## Activity 2 · check your answers {#activity-2-check}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.lever-box}
[A · cyclohexane + methanol, 298.15 K, z₁ = 0.25]{.label}

Curvature 0.114 > 0, yet TPD = −0.0596 at w₁ = 0.900: metastable, it splits. Liquids 0.177 and 0.876; fraction of the cyclohexane-rich liquid (0.25 − 0.177)/(0.876 − 0.177) = **0.104**.
:::

::: {.lever-box}
[B · crystallizer]{.label}

x₁ = 0.1437 at 298.15 K, 0.0878 at 285 K. Crystallized 0.0612 mol per mol feed: **42.6 %**. Ideal design: 0.302 → 0.212, 37.8 %, with a feed 2.1 times richer. 285 K is 2.8 K below the lowest measured row (287.8 K).
:::
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.lever-box}
[C · ranking, from 0.795]{.label}

| Error | Conversion | Change |
|---|---:|---:|
| (i) constant Δ<sub>r</sub>H | 0.498 | −0.297 |
| (ii) pressure term omitted | 0.996 | +0.201 |
| (iii) S/C = 4 | 0.869 | +0.074 |
| (iv) with K<sub>φ</sub> | 0.794 | −0.001 |

KCl with RT/F: **half**, 108.0 mV instead of 216.0 mV.
:::
:::

## Audit: what the checks found {#audit-debrief}

| Script | Symptom | Check that fails | Cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lab 05 | binodal 0.519 / 0.519; TPD 0 at w = z | binodal, TPD minimum | solver started between the phases; TPD searched from the feed only |
| Lab 10 | x₁(298.15) = 0.108 | prediction; W off the minimum | γ₁ evaluated at x₂ = 1; objective in ln γ, not ln x |
| Lab 12 | conversion 0.498, converged | ln K₁ and ln K₂ | K from Δ<sub>r</sub>H fixed at 298 K |
| Lab 13 | EMF 118.3 / 108.0 mV | both EMF checks | a = mγ±, not (mγ±)² |

None of the four failed by crashing or by not converging. Each failed a thermodynamic check that an independent calculation could make.

## Exam-style problem {#exam-problem}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
::: {.prompt}
A colleague fits ln γ₁ = (W/RT)x₂² to naphthalene solubility in benzene and reports "W = −522 J/mol: benzene is a better-than-ideal solvent". (a) Reproduce the claim from the data in Lab 10 E. (b) Is the claim supported? (c) What would you report instead, and what one measurement would settle the sign?
:::
:::
::: {.column width="40%" .rule-notes}
[25 minutes · alone]{.label}

Answer in this order: equation, assumptions with their size, numbers, check, conclusion and its limit.

You may use the labs. State every number you take from them.
:::
::::

## Exam-style problem: a model answer {#exam-answer}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
**(a)** ln(x₁γ₁) = −(Δ<sub>fus</sub>H/R)(1/T − 1/T<sub>m</sub>), ΔC<sub>p</sub> neglected. With the article's DSC data (355.04 K, 20.87 kJ/mol) and all ten rows, least squares in ln x₁: W = −522 J/mol, RMSE 0.008.

**(b)** No. With the NIST data (353.39 K, 19.0 kJ/mol), W = +238 J/mol. The two fusion sets differ by about their stated uncertainty, and the sign of W follows them. x₁ at 298.15 K is 0.289 or 0.287 either way.
:::
::: {.column width="46%" .rule-notes}
**(c)** Report: near-ideal, |ln γ₁| ≤ 0.13 between 286 and 326 K with either fusion data set; x₁(298.15 K) = 0.287 to 0.289. That spread is the **difference between the two fusion data sets considered**, not a full uncertainty: the solubility data and the model form add to it. Do not report the sign of W.

To settle the sign: a measurement that does not pass through the solid, such as H<sup>E</sup> or VLE of liquid naphthalene + benzene, or Δ<sub>fus</sub>H measured to better than ±0.5 kJ/mol.

[Both W and x₁(298.15 K) come from a fit to all ten rows, and 298.15 K lies inside the data range. That is calibration (rung 1), not held-out validation. A held-out check would refit without some rows and predict them.]{.q}
:::
::::

## How answers are marked {#marking}

::: {.mistakes}
::: {}
**Equation and reference state (25 %).** The right equilibrium condition, with standard states and units stated.
:::
::: {}
**Assumptions with their size (20 %).** Not "assume ideal", but "Φ = 1 changes ln γ by 0.011".
:::
::: {}
**Numbers that can be checked (25 %).** Intermediate values, units, and a balance or limit that closes.
:::
::: {}
**Conclusion and its limit (30 %).** What the evidence supports, which rung it reached, what would raise it.
:::
:::

A correct number with no limit stated earns less than a well-argued answer with an arithmetic slip.

## Summary {#summary}

::: {.summary3}
::: {}
[One condition]{.label}
Equal chemical potential, in six forms. What changes is the reference state and the model.
:::
::: {}
[Evidence]{.label}
Calibration, consistency, held-out, independent property, different method. A claim is only as strong as its highest rung.
:::
::: {}
[Code]{.label}
Converging is not checking. Recompute one quantity independently, close a balance, test a limit.
:::
:::

**Session question:** the strongest evidence in this course was held-out data and independent properties: tie lines the fit did not use, LLE against a VLE fit, a second fusion data set. Where we had neither, the honest answer was to say what the data cannot decide.
